task_evals.prompt: Use research-paper-pilot on this project. I have forgotten what it is about and need to write it up. Start from scratch.
task_evals.setup: A small repository with at least 12 dated git commits by two authors, a RESULTS.md that lists three experiments and their headline numbers, a results/ directory with one JSON file per experiment, a README that mentions a document NOTES_v2.md which does not exist on disk, and a paper/ directory with a half-written main.tex.
task_evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/inventory_project.py and writes paper/PROJECT_INVENTORY.md. Reads README, RESULTS.md, paper/ and git history before asking anything, then asks the user one question at a time and only about what the files cannot answer. Writes paper/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md from the template with a one-sentence identity, the question, hypotheses, claims with status and evidence pointers, and a Missing documents entry naming NOTES_v2.md. Produces a plain-language explainer with a glossary and a dated story arc, plus one worked example of a real data item. Ends with the four-part output contract and a LAB_LOG entry.
assertions: PROJECT_INVENTORY.md exists and lists the git authors with commit counts
PROJECT_CONTEXT.md exists and has a one-line Status line
NOTES_v2.md is reported as cited but absent
Each claim in the explainer has a status from the ladder (established, supported, equivocal, retired, exploratory) and a file pointer
No result file was modified
The reply ends with files written, decisions taken, open items and next recommended mode

task_evals.prompt: Check the numbers in paper/main.tex against our results before I send it.
task_evals.setup: paper/main.tex states 'accuracy improved from 0.71 to 0.80' in the Results section as a literal and uses \accA for the same quantity elsewhere. paper/numbers.tex defines \accA as 0.78, taken from results/exp3.json. The abstract also contains a literal 1.07 that appears in no result file.
task_evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/check_numbers.py with the numbers file and results directory. Reports 0.80 as a literal that is not a macro and appears in no result file or differs from the macro, and reports 1.07 as unsourced. Does not edit results/exp3.json. Proposes replacing literals with macros and, where the macro value disagrees with the prose, flags the disagreement for the author rather than silently choosing a number. Records the decision in LAB_LOG.md and ends with the four-part output contract.
assertions: 0.80 is flagged as a stale or non-macro literal
1.07 is flagged as appearing in no result file
The disagreement between 0.80 and the 0.78 macro is shown to the user
results/exp3.json is unchanged
No number is changed without the user being told

task_evals.prompt: Humanize this paragraph from the discussion section. It has to keep the hedge and the citation.
task_evals.setup: Input paragraph: 'It is worth noting that, in today's rapidly evolving landscape, our method may improve calibration on held-out data (Smith et al., 2021), showcasing its pivotal role. Furthermore, it is not merely an optimisation, but a paradigm shift. In conclusion, these results underscore the importance of calibration.' The user states that numbers and citations are already frozen.
task_evals.expected_output: Reads references/humanize.md, edits structure and staging before vocabulary, removes the throat-clearing opener, the inflated significance, the not-merely-but construction and the closing loop, and keeps 'may improve' and the citation 'Smith et al., 2021' unchanged. Runs scripts/verify_rewrite.py on source and rewrite and shows that it reports no DROPPED or ADDED facts. States that this edits style and does not certify authorship. Ends with the four-part output contract.
assertions: The word 'may' (or an equivalent hedge) survives next to the improvement claim
The citation key or text 'Smith et al., 2021' survives exactly
verify_rewrite.py was run and its result is shown
At least three AI patterns from the source paragraph are removed
No new factual claim is added
The response does not promise to evade AI detectors

task_evals.prompt: Rewrite this results paragraph so a reviewer outside our group can follow it. We do not want a glossary in the paper.
task_evals.setup: Input paragraph: 'On S3, arm A beats arm B by 2.1 points (A 4.2, B 6.3, C 6.0; 5 seeds, 95% CI 1.4 to 2.8), so C rules out the warm-up story; the shield holds on S1 to S3 and the canary stays flat.' paper/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md has a glossary: arm A = model trained with label smoothing; arm B = baseline with no smoothing; arm C = control with the same warm-up schedule as A but no smoothing; S1 to S3 = the blur, noise and contrast shifts; shield = the finding that the gain survives all three shifts; canary = an untouched reference model evaluated with every run.
task_evals.expected_output: Reads references/glossary-and-plain-language.md. Replaces every letter code and metaphor name with a plain description taken from the glossary, introduces the control by its role (it rules out the warm-up schedule as the cause) before reporting its result, states the comparison in words before the numbers, keeps the numbers that carry the claim, and either keeps the remaining values or says they move to a table. Runs scripts/prose_gate.py --academic on the result and shows no label codes in the reader-load block. Does not add a glossary to the paper. Ends with the output contract.
assertions: No 'arm A', 'arm B', 'arm C', 'S1', 'S2', 'S3', 'shield' or 'canary' remains in the rewritten paragraph
The control's purpose (ruling out the warm-up schedule) is stated before or with its result
The values 2.1, 4.2, 6.3, 6.0, 5 seeds and the interval 1.4 to 2.8 are either kept or explicitly moved to a table, none silently dropped
No number is changed
No glossary is added to the paper
prose_gate.py was run and its reader-load result is shown
